page: Microsoft Azure E2ads_v5 is an entry-tier, memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing the x86_64 architecture. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at frequencies up to 3.525 GHz, it allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs across a single physical core with multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture comprises 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, backed by instruction extensions including AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per-core allocation, along with 81 GB of temporary local SSD storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread execution, highlighted by a top-quartile stress-ng single-core score of 2,701.48 and mid-range performance in gzip compression (28.37 GB/sec) and single-core Geekbench (1,430.0). However, overall parallel capacity is constrained by the two-vCPU ceiling. Multi-core Geekbench (1,739.0) and multi-core stress-ng fall into lower percentile tiers, while uncached memory read bandwidth (34.27 GB/sec) and write bandwidth (22.5 GB/sec) reflect the narrow memory bus allocated to smaller VM shapes.

By delivering an expansive 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio alongside integrated high-speed local disk storage, the E2ads_v5 achieves cost efficiency for memory-dependent tasks that do not demand extensive core counts. Tradeoffs include low overall transactional throughput and limited multi-threaded scaling in compute-heavy or large-scale compilation tasks.

The configuration fits small in-memory caching nodes, development or staging relational databases, lightweight background ETL workers, batch processing scripts, and microservice backends that require a comfortable memory cushion without incurring the overhead of broader multi-core provisioning.
description: Microsoft Azure E2ads_v5 is an entry-level memory-optimized instance built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7763 processor, delivering 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single physical core operating up to 3.525 GHz. The configuration provides 16 GB of system RAM, maintaining a high 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio, alongside an integrated 81 GB local SSD for high-speed scratch space and temporary file caching. Single-thread processing registers respectable benchmark execution, led by strong single-core stress-ng performance and average single-thread decompression speeds. However, with only two virtual threads, multi-threaded throughput and aggregate memory bandwidth are strictly constrained, resulting in lower scores on multi-core Geekbench suites and database transactional operations. The instance offers resource efficiency for applications prioritizing memory footprint over multi-threaded compute. It is suitable for small in-memory caches, lightweight database replicas, background ETL tasks, staging environments, and single-threaded batch processing services.
